facts.text: Halton Hills got its name after a 1973 referendum changed the original title, Town of North Halton, to honor the region's heritage.
Glen Williams, founded in 1825 beside the Credit River, still hosts many 1840s and 1850s buildings that echo its early settler roots.
Norval once welcomed author Lucy Maud Montgomery, whose Anne of Green Gables fame ties the town to Canadian literary history.
The Grand Trunk Railway first reached Halton Hills in 1856, establishing stations at Acton and Georgetown that linked the town to the wider rail network.
The Niagara Escarpment cuts through Halton Hills, shaping its rolling landscape and creating a natural border between forest zones.
Environment and Climate Change Canada runs a climate station at Georgetown, providing long‑term weather data for the town’s two distinct zones.
